policies.name: conv2d
policies.note: The convolution derivative is a joint input/weight/bias formula containing both full tensors. The generated save guard does not condition these joint-formula inputs on individual gradients. Native bias is a separate add operation.

policies.name: avg_pool2d
policies.note: The actual backward schema receives full self; value-independent mathematics alone does not justify skipping its SavedVariable version check.

policies.name: max_pool2d
policies.note: The floating output is not the saved result. Native argmax/config allocation must remain live independently of public tensor release.

policies.name: matmul
policies.note: Dense CPU matmul is CompositeImplicitAutograd. Its generic joint matmul_backward derivative must not be applied as a dense save policy: _matmul_impl dispatches through dot/mv/mm/bmm. Each saves the opposite operand if the corresponding input requires gradient. Fold/expand followed by reshape can create a fresh-storage copy, whose version is independent of the original input. A uniform native save-original policy is conservative but can reject mutations accepted by pinned PyTorch. Actual path probes remain necessary.

policies.name: index_select
policies.note: Self sizes are saved as metadata. Current wire indices are copied into immutable native config; a mutable int64 Tensor API is not implemented.

policies.name: gather
policies.note: gather_backward receives full self and indices. The generated formula saves both, including a version check on self. Wire indices are currently immutable config.

policies.name: cat
policies.note: Metadata and gradient edges are separate from saved values.

policies.name: stack
policies.note: Metadata and gradient edges are separate from saved values.

policies.name: scatter_add
policies.note: Neither self nor source tensor values occur in the two derivative expressions. Source/index shape mismatch can still produce a delayed backward error.

policies.name: index_add
policies.note: Although source.dim() becomes metadata, expand_as(source) still contains a Tensor reference. The generator therefore saves source; changing it invalidates backward.
